quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: The DMV will mail an advisory letter to adult drivers who get ____ points on their driving record within 12 months.

options.text: Between 6 and 11
Between 8 and 10
12 or more

questions.correctAnswerText: Between 6 and 11
questions.explanation: Adult drivers get an advisory letter if they earn 6 to 11 points in 12 months. Drivers under 18 get the same letter if they earn 1 to 5 points in 12 months.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Get ready to stop if needed.
Keep driving at the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill or around a curve. A car might be stopped in the road. Slow down when you reach a hill or curve so you can stop if needed.

questions.question: Which road is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A road in a neighborhood
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze before other parts of the road and thaw out later. On cold, wet days, these spots become icy and slippery.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: You cannot pass another vehicle.
You can pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if no cars are coming toward you. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes on and off.
Press and hold the brake pedal hard.
Do not use the brakes and let the car slow down on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal hard.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal hard and keep it pressed on snowy or icy roads. The ABS will pump the brakes automatically, faster than you can do it by hand.

questions.question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not count on the other driver making room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the other driver will drive at the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not count on the other driver making room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you space to pass, even if you use your turn signal. You must make sure it is safe before you pass.

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane with two lanes going your direction. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. A driver behind you wants to go faster. You should:

options.text: Stay in your lane so traffic flows smoothly.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane for faster driving, passing, and left turns. Use the right lane for slower driving, entering the road, and right turns.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are driving in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop before you reach a school bus that is picking up or dropping off children. This applies whether you are traveling in the same direction or the opposite direction.

questions.question: Your license can be suspended if you are under 21 and drive with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot have any alcohol in their system. Even a tiny amount of alcohol will result in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: This red and white sign means you should:

options.text: Stop completely and look both ways before going.
Let traffic on the road ahead of you go first.
Drive at a steady speed and watch for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic on the road ahead of you go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign tells you to slow down and be ready to stop if needed. You do not have the right-of-way. Let any vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians pass before you go.

questions.question: How can you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly at the right side of the road.
Keep your eyes on the center line.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly at the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights. Then continue looking ahead to see where the other vehicle is.

questions.question: When should you leave extra space between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, or vehicles with trailers may not see you behind them. Leave more space between your car and these vehicles. This also helps you see the road ahead around the sides of the large vehicle.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid a dangerous driving situation?

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Pay attention to everything around your vehicle—in front, on the sides, and behind. This helps you spot problems and change your speed or position when needed.

questions.question: When parallel parking, how close should your wheels be to the curb?

options.text: Within two feet of the curb.
Within 18 inches of the curb.
Within one foot of the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 18 inches of the curb.
questions.explanation: Your wheels must be within 18 inches of the curb when parking. Only park where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: What should you do if an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights?

options.text: Look at the center of the road.
Look at the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see enough of the road to stay safe. Do not keep your high beams on as payback.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn it and keep it by following the rules.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning when driving in rain?

options.text: Drive at a speed for normal conditions.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car skids.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose contact with the wet road and slide on water. Driving slower in wet conditions prevents this problem.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent a crash.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crosswalk.

questions.question: When driving on a one-way street, when can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: When you speed up before turning.
When traffic moves to the right.
When traffic moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street if traffic moves to the left and there is no sign stopping you. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and keep going without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road is slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians crossing any street. For safety, yield to pedestrians whether the crosswalk is marked or not.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns you that you are leaving a one-way highway. Traffic will soon be moving in both directions.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians walking along the road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Pedestrians must not cross here.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs tell drivers about road conditions. This sign alerts you that pedestrians may be crossing ahead. Stop and wait until pedestrians have fully crossed.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones?

options.text: Fines in work zones are the same as fines for normal traffic violations.
You must "Slow for the Cone Zone."
Slow down only if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must "Slow for the Cone Zone."
questions.explanation: Slow down in work zones. Keep safety in mind for drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and road workers.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle must turn or pull off the road when ____ vehicles are in line behind it.

options.text: At least four
Five or more
Eight or more

questions.correctAnswerText: Five or more
questions.explanation: When driving a slow-moving vehicle, pull off the road if five or more vehicles are behind you. Safely return to the road after other vehicles pass.

questions.question: If your car skids out of control, you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes lightly.
Stay off the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes if your vehicle skids. Steer to regain control. Once the vehicle is stable, drive safely.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is turning left:

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic. Be ready to see a bicyclist using the left lane when making a left turn.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, drive:

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, use the lane closest to the centerline. Begin your turn just before reaching the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first legal lane.
